extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers (authors and reviewers), conference organizers and program chairs interested in reproducibility practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for making machine learning conference papers reproducible (NeurIPS 2019 program): code submission policy, a community reproducibility challenge, and a paper-level checklist used at submission and camera-ready stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of reproducibility (and related terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducible work consists of re-doing an experiment using the same data and same analytical tools; Replicable work considers different data; Robust work assumes the same data but different analysis (e.g., reimplementation); Generalisable work leads to the same conclusions despite different data and different analytical tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report adopts these definitions and focuses primarily on 'Reproducibility' (same data & tools). Use these distinctions when designing, reporting, and evaluating experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to the same training data / data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of access to the same training data or differences in data distribution is a major obstacle to reproducing ML experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When data are confidential (e.g., privacy-sensitive), mitigate by providing results on open-source benchmark datasets in addition to confidential data; explicitly document data availability and any distributional differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of model and training procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Misspecification or under-specification of the model or training procedure undermines reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear description of the mathematical setting, algorithm, model, and the procedural details needed to re-run experiments (architecture, optimization, preprocessing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of code
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of availability of the code necessary to run the experiments, or errors in the code, impedes reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NeurIPS policy: authors are highly encouraged to submit code; expectation (but not requirement) that accepted papers presenting experiments with a new algorithm submit accompanying code by camera-ready. Authors may include code as supplementary material (policy example: up to 100MB). Reviewers were asked to record whether code was provided and whether they looked at it or found it useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of evaluation metrics and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Under-specification of the metrics used to report results (lack of a clear definition of the specific measures or statistics) harms reproducibility and interpretability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define measures and statistics used to report results so others can reproduce the reported numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper statistical analysis and uncertainty quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper use of statistics (e.g., claiming significance without proper tests or using wrong tests) and lack of uncertainty quantification are common reproducibility problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate statistical testing and routinely quantify uncertainty (e.g., error bars, central tendency and variation like mean and stddev). The checklist specifically asks for clearly defined error bars and reporting of central tendency & variation for results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid selective reporting and adaptive overfitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective reporting of results and ignoring the danger of adaptive overfitting reduce reliability of conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report experimental selection procedures, search over hyperparameters, and negative or unsuccessful runs where relevant; avoid reporting only the best cherry-picked runs without documenting the search process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must match evidence (avoid over-claiming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over-claiming results (drawing conclusions beyond the evidence) or mismatch between hypothesis and presented claim undermines scientific validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure conclusions are supported by the experiments and analyses reported; be conservative in claims when evidence is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient experimental exploration and repetitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient number of experiments, inadequate hyperparameter exploration, or insufficient random-seed trials make results fragile and hard to reproduce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct and report enough trials (e.g., multiple random seeds), and thorough hyperparameter searches to support statements about method improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Science practices (sharing artifacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Science — making code, data, and scientific communications publicly available — is a core factor to improve reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, publish code and data, and use public platforms to share reproducibility reports and artifacts so others can inspect and build on the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code submission policy specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS 2019 policy excerpt: authors may submit supplementary material (e.g., proofs, derivations, data, or source code). The conference 'highly encourage[d]' code submission and 'expect[ed] (but not require[d])' accompanying code for accepted papers presenting experiments with a new algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code submission was voluntary at initial submission but expected by camera-ready for accepted experimental algorithm papers; reviewers were asked whether code was provided and whether they inspected it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist item: clear description of mathematical setting/algorithm/model
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist question: 'A clear description of the mathematical setting, algorithm, and/or model.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an expectation for nearly all submissions; the authors reported ~97% compliance, and the checklist required Yes/No/NA plus optional comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist item: experimental run descriptions for figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist question (for all figures and tables that present empirical results): include a description of how experiments were run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the experimental protocol used to generate figures and tables (datasets, splits, preprocessing, model training details, hardware, runtimes) so results in figures/tables can be reproduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist item: clearly defined error bars
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, include error bars with definition (e.g., stddev, confidence intervals) to reflect variability; note that many papers marked error bars as 'not applicable' even while defining metrics—authors should carefully consider applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist item: report central tendency and variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist question: 'A description of results with central tendency (e.g., mean) & variation (e.g., stddev).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report summary statistics (means, medians where appropriate) together with measures of dispersion so readers can assess variability and robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist format and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The ML reproducibility checklist (v1.2) was implemented on the submission platform; each question had multiple-choice answers (Yes/No/Not applicable) and an optional open comment field. Authors were obliged to fill it at initial submission and at camera-ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the checklist at both submission and camera-ready enables tracking changes made in response to reviews; reviewers could indicate whether they found the checklist answers useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility challenge practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The NeurIPS reproducibility challenge solicited independent verification reports for accepted papers, producing public reproducibility reports (often including reimplementation code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility reports should give detailed, nuanced accounts of what was reproduced and at what fidelity rather than a single binary 'reproducible' score; making reports public creates examples and archival evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer engagement with artifacts (code usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers were surveyed about code: whether it was provided, whether they looked at it, and whether it was useful in guiding their review; availability of code at submission correlated positively with reviewer scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reviewers to check for artifact availability and to consult code when provided; record artifact interactions in the review metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tooling recommendation: use of software containers
rubrics_metrics.description: Software containers (e.g., Docker) can encapsulate operating system components, code and data into a single package and standardization of such tools would help sharing and improve ease of reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the program did not prescribe specific tooling, containers are recommended as a practical mechanism to package reproducible environments.
